Study 2 replaces the smooth surfaces of DDM-5, the model retained in Study 1
(`2_modelcomparison.qmd`), with linear effects of task difficulty and illusion
strength, so that every effect, and every participant's sensitivity to the
illusion, is one interpretable coefficient. This script has two parts:

- **Model Specification**: how the linear predictors were chosen, from the
  Study 1 fits. It reads only their prediction files (`./hpc predict`, then
  `./hpc pull predictions`), never a fit, like `2_modelcomparison.qmd`.
- **Convergence**, and what follows, once the linear models are fitted.

## Loading

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| error: false

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(gt)

# restore_units(): the Z-scored predictors of the Study 1 fits back in raw units
source(if (dir.exists("server")) "server/predictions.R" else "analysis/server/predictions.R")
# The model registry: Study 2's linear subrange (igc_linear_ranges) and the
# linear models' entries
source(if (dir.exists("server")) "server/models.R" else "analysis/server/models.R")

path <- if (dir.exists("models")) "models/" else "analysis/models/"
pred_path <- paste0(path, "predictions/")
data_path <- if (dir.exists("../data")) "../data/" else "data/"

# The prediction files of Study 2's linear models, per illusion. They are made
# on the cluster from the combined fits (`./hpc combine`, `./hpc predict`, then
# `./hpc pull predictions`), like Study 1's, and never computed here. Until the
# full fits exist, the Müller-Lyer one is the 50-participant test of 2026-11-25
# (job 11841190, the coding without a gap, server/AGENT.md 6.15), in a
# directory of its own (pulled with IGC_LOCAL_MODELS, server/hpc). The test of
# 2026-11-24, with the gap, is in test_lin_ddm5_20261124_nutpie/ (6.14). The
# Vertical-Horizontal one is the same test (submitted 2026-11-25), and the
# Ebbinghaus one too (submitted 2026-11-26), in the same directory. An illusion
# with no file yet is left out.
linear_files <- c(
  MullerLyer = paste0(path, "test_lin_ddm5_20261125_nutpie/predictions/lin_ddm5_mullerlyer_MullerLyer.rds"),
  VerticalHorizontal = paste0(path, "test_lin_ddm5_20261125_nutpie/predictions/",
                              "lin_ddm5_verticalhorizontal_VerticalHorizontal.rds"),
  Ebbinghaus = paste0(path, "test_lin_ddm5_20261125_nutpie/predictions/lin_ddm5_ebbinghaus_Ebbinghaus.rds")
)

illusions <- c(MullerLyer = "Müller-Lyer", VerticalHorizontal = "Vertical-Horizontal",
               Ebbinghaus = "Ebbinghaus")

# The trials, as fit_model.R reads them (it takes them from GitHub, which is
# the same files)
df <- map_dfr(1:3, \(i) read.csv(paste0(data_path, "illusion_part", i, ".csv"))) |>
  mutate(Illusion_Difference = abs(Illusion_Difference))

# The tables, in one style, with the numbers centred in their cells (side by
# side, right-aligned numbers in cells of a similar colour read as one cell).
# R² cells are coloured on one scale throughout, from pale orange (0.7 and
# below) to green (1), as in the figure of the transformations, and changes in
# R² from red (worse) to green (better); values beyond a scale take the colour
# of its end.
gt_style <- function(tab) {
  tab |>
    cols_align("center", columns = where(is.numeric)) |>
    tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), heading.title.font.size = px(15),
                heading.subtitle.font.size = px(12), column_labels.font.weight = "bold",
                row_group.font.weight = "bold", data_row.padding = px(4),
                source_notes.font.size = px(11)) |>
    opt_align_table_header(align = "left")
}
squished <- function(palette, domain) {
  pal <- scales::col_numeric(palette, domain)
  \(x) pal(pmin(pmax(x, domain[1]), domain[2]))
}
colour_r2 <- function(tab, columns) {
  data_color(tab, columns = {{ columns }}, fn = squished(c("#FFF3E0", "#66BB6A"), c(0.7, 1)))
}
colour_change <- function(tab, columns) {
  data_color(tab, columns = {{ columns }},
             fn = squished(c("#E57373", "white", "#66BB6A"), c(-0.03, 0.03)))
}
```

## Model Specification

### The Study 1 Surfaces

The linear models are specified from DDM-5's parameter surfaces in Study 1:
for each parameter, its population-level value over a 40 x 40 grid of task
difficulty x illusion strength (the heatmaps of `2_modelcomparison.qmd`). A
linear model acts on each parameter's linear predictor, so the surfaces are
taken back to that scale, through the link function of the parameter.

```{r}
# The link of each parameter of cogmod_ddm() (cogmod::cogmod_ddm()$link_*):
# identity for the drift, softplus for the boundary and the drift variability,
# logit for the bias and log for the non-decision time. Each is applied as its
# inverse, from the parameter back to its linear predictor.
ddm_links <- list(mu = identity, boundary = \(x) log(expm1(x)), bias = qlogis,
                  ndt = log, sigmadrift = \(x) log(expm1(x)))
ddm_labels <- c(mu = "Drift", boundary = "Boundary", bias = "Bias", ndt = "NDT",
                sigmadrift = "Drift Variability")

surfaces <- imap_dfr(illusions, \(label, ill) {
  h <- readRDS(paste0(pred_path, "gam_ddm5_", tolower(ill), "_", ill, ".rds"))$heatmaps |>
    restore_units(ill)
  h$Link <- NA_real_
  for (p in names(ddm_links)) {
    h$Link[h$Parameter == p] <- ddm_links[[p]](h$Predicted[h$Parameter == p])
  }
  h
})

surfaces |>
  summarise(Difference_min = min(Illusion_Difference), Difference_max = max(Illusion_Difference),
            Strength_max = max(abs(Illusion_Strength)), .by = Illusion_Type) |>
  mutate(Illusion = illusions[Illusion_Type], .keep = "unused", .before = 1) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The Study 1 surfaces",
             subtitle = "Range of the 40 x 40 grid of each illusion, in raw units") |>
  tab_spanner("Difference", starts_with("Difference")) |>
  cols_label(Difference_min = "from", Difference_max = "to", Strength_max = "Strength (±)") |>
  fmt_number(starts_with("Difference"), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_number(Strength_max, decimals = 2, drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE) |>
  gt_style()
```

### The Three Ranges of the Predictors

Task difficulty and illusion strength are used over three nested ranges
(`server/AGENT.md` §6.17):

- **The full range**: every value shown in any study. The Study 1 models are
  fitted to every trial, over this range.
- **The reliable predictor space** (the reliable subrange): the full range
  less the values that only one study showed. Every prediction and figure, of
  Study 1 and Study 2, is made over it (`plot_ranges` in
  `server/predictions.R`).
- **The linear subrange**: the part of the reliable predictor space that the
  linear models of Study 2 are fitted on, where the effects of the two
  predictors are taken to be close enough to linear (`igc_linear_ranges` in
  `server/models.R`). It is still to be refined, and for now it is the whole
  reliable predictor space.

### The Full Range, Study by Study

The studies did not all show the same stimuli. They used three designs (table
below). Validation, the first, showed the strongest illusions, and on
Müller-Lyer and Ebbinghaus also the largest differences. EEG and Reliability
used a narrower grid. The four later studies (International, Suggestibility,
Phenomenological Control and Self-Association) used the main one, which
contains the EEG and Reliability grid. Every study showed 8 levels of difference
and 8 or 10 of strength. The levels that only Validation showed were seen by
about 250 participants, in about 4,000 trials per level, against 10,000 to
27,000 trials per level elsewhere. What is estimated there rests on one study,
which the GAMs of Study 1, with no effect of study, cannot tell apart from what
is particular to it.

```{r}
# The stimuli of each study, per illusion: the range of the difference and of
# the absolute strength, their numbers of levels, and the share of the trials
# outside the reliable predictor space (plot_ranges, checked against the data
# in the next chunk)
study_order <- c("Validation", "EEG", "Reliability", "International", "Suggestibility", "PCS",
                 "SelfAssociation")
df |>
  mutate(Study = factor(sub("^IllusionGame", "", Dataset), levels = study_order),
         Reliable = in_plot_range(first(Illusion_Type), Illusion_Difference, Illusion_Strength),
         .by = Illusion_Type) |>
  summarise(Participants = n_distinct(Participant), Trials = n(),
            Difference_from = min(Illusion_Difference), Difference_to = max(Illusion_Difference),
            Difference_levels = n_distinct(Illusion_Difference),
            Strength_max = max(abs(Illusion_Strength)), Strength_levels = n_distinct(abs(Illusion_Strength)),
            Outside = mean(!Reliable), .by = c(Illusion_Type, Study)) |>
  mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions)) |>
  arrange(Illusion, Study) |>
  select(Illusion, Study, Participants, Trials, Difference_from, Difference_to, Difference_levels,
         Strength_max, Strength_levels, Outside) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Illusion") |>
  tab_header(title = "The full range, study by study",
             subtitle = "The stimuli each study showed, and the share of its trials outside the reliable predictor space") |>
  tab_spanner("Difference", starts_with("Difference")) |>
  tab_spanner("Strength", starts_with("Strength")) |>
  cols_label(Difference_from = "from", Difference_to = "to", Difference_levels = "levels",
             Strength_max = "±", Strength_levels = "levels", Outside = "Trials outside") |>
  fmt_integer(c(Participants, Trials)) |>
  fmt_number(starts_with("Difference_"), decimals = 3, drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE) |>
  fmt_integer(ends_with("_levels")) |>
  fmt_number(Strength_max, decimals = 2, drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE) |>
  fmt_percent(Outside, decimals = 0) |>
  tab_source_note("Strength levels count a strength and its opposite as one; PCS is Phenomenological Control.") |>
  gt_style()
```

### The Reliable Predictor Space

The figures and the linear fits are therefore limited to a reliable predictor
space, by one rule for the three illusions: at each end of each predictor, the
most extreme values that together hold less than 5% of the illusion's trials
are left out. The difference is kept from its 5th to its 95th percentile, and
the absolute strength up to its 95th percentile. On all three illusions this is
exactly the range of the main design. What it leaves out is the levels that
only Validation showed, 38% to 53% of that study's trials, and none of the
other studies' trials. Every curve and heatmap of Study 1 and Study 2 is drawn
over this space (`plot_ranges` in `server/predictions.R`, which the code below
checks against the data).

```{r}
# The reliable predictor space at threshold p: the difference from its p-th to
# its (1 - p)-th quantile and the absolute strength up to its (1 - p)-th, over
# every trial of the illusion (the difference is absolute already)
reliable_space <- function(p = 0.05) {
  df |>
    summarise(Difference_from = quantile(Illusion_Difference, p, type = 1),
              Difference_to = quantile(Illusion_Difference, 1 - p, type = 1),
              Strength = quantile(abs(Illusion_Strength), 1 - p, type = 1),
              .by = Illusion_Type) |>
    arrange(Illusion_Type)
}
space <- reliable_space(0.05)

# The thresholds that give the same space
thresholds <- seq(0.01, 0.15, by = 0.01)
same_space <- thresholds[map_lgl(thresholds, \(p) isTRUE(all.equal(reliable_space(p), space)))]

# plot_ranges must be this space: it is what the prediction files are made over
for (ill in names(illusions)) {
  r <- plot_ranges[[ill]]
  s <- filter(space, Illusion_Type == ill)
  if (is.null(r) || !isTRUE(all.equal(c(r$difference, max(r$strength)),
                                      c(s$Difference_from, s$Difference_to, s$Strength)))) {
    stop("plot_ranges in server/predictions.R is not the reliable predictor space of ", ill,
         ": update it, then re-run `./hpc predict`.")
  }
}

df |>
  left_join(space, by = "Illusion_Type") |>
  mutate(In = Illusion_Difference >= Difference_from - 1e-9 & Illusion_Difference <= Difference_to + 1e-9 &
           abs(Illusion_Strength) <= Strength + 1e-9) |>
  summarise(Difference_from = first(Difference_from), Difference_to = first(Difference_to),
            Strength = first(Strength), Kept = mean(In),
            Out_Studies = paste(sort(unique(sub("^IllusionGame", "", Dataset[!In]))), collapse = ", "),
            .by = Illusion_Type) |>
  mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions)) |>
  arrange(Illusion) |>
  select(Illusion, Difference_from, Difference_to, Strength, Kept, Out_Studies) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The reliable predictor space",
             subtitle = "At each end of each predictor, the values holding less than 5% of the trials left out") |>
  tab_spanner("Difference", starts_with("Difference")) |>
  cols_label(Difference_from = "from", Difference_to = "to", Strength = "Strength (±)",
             Kept = "Trials kept", Out_Studies = "Studies of the trials left out") |>
  fmt_number(starts_with("Difference"), decimals = 3, drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE) |>
  fmt_number(Strength, decimals = 2, drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE) |>
  fmt_percent(Kept, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_source_note(paste0("The same space for every threshold from ", 100 * min(same_space), "% to ",
                         100 * max(same_space), "%.")) |>
  gt_style()
```

### The Linear Subrange

The linear models are fitted over a linear subrange of each illusion, within
the reliable predictor space. This is the set of stimuli over which the effects
of the two predictors are taken to be close enough to linear for a linear model
to stand in for DDM-5's surfaces. It is set in `igc_linear_ranges` in
`server/models.R`, and the registry's linear models take their range from it.

**The linear subrange is still to be refined.** For now it is the whole
reliable predictor space, on all three illusions. With the coding chosen below,
the least linear parameter keeps an R² of .87 to .89 over it. A narrower
subrange would trade trials for linearity, and the criterion for that is not
decided. The boxes drawn in Study 1 for the signed coding of strength (Müller-Lyer
0.1–0.4 x ±30, drawn by eye) are candidates (`server/AGENT.md` §6.17). A
narrower subrange shows in the figures: the linear model's lines stop short of
the edges of the reliable predictor space, and `2_modelcomparison.qmd`
outlines the subrange on its heatmaps.

For Müller-Lyer, the reliable predictor space starts at a difference of 0.045,
the hardest level of the main design (8% of its trials), where the range of
Study 1 started at 0.05. That level is the least linear part of its surfaces:
without it, the worst parameter of the coding retained below is at .917 rather
than .887 (the non-decision time), as the surfaces bend most at the hardest
discriminations. It is one candidate for a narrower linear subrange.

```{r}
# The linear subrange, in raw units: difference from-to, and the largest
# absolute strength (igc_linear_ranges in server/models.R). For now the
# reliable predictor space on all three illusions. It must lie within the
# reliable predictor space, as must the range of every linear model in the
# registry (a variant may set its own).
linear_ranges <- igc_linear_ranges
within_reliable <- function(r, illusion) {
  p <- plot_ranges[[illusion]]
  !is.null(p) && r$difference[1] >= p$difference[1] - 1e-9 && r$difference[2] <= p$difference[2] + 1e-9 &&
    r$strength <= max(p$strength) + 1e-9
}
for (ill in names(linear_ranges)) {
  if (!within_reliable(linear_ranges[[ill]], ill)) {
    stop("igc_linear_ranges in server/models.R is not within the reliable predictor space of ", ill, ".")
  }
}
for (m in names(igc_models)) {
  l <- igc_models[[m]]$linear
  if (!is.null(l) && !within_reliable(l, igc_models[[m]]$illusion)) {
    stop(m, ": its range in server/models.R is not within the reliable predictor space.")
  }
}

# The three ranges side by side, with the trials in each
range_row <- function(ill, d, s) {
  inside <- df$Illusion_Type == ill & df$Illusion_Difference >= d[1] - 1e-9 &
    df$Illusion_Difference <= d[2] + 1e-9 & abs(df$Illusion_Strength) <= s + 1e-9
  tibble(Difference = paste0(signif(d[1], 3), "–", signif(d[2], 3)), Strength = paste0("±", signif(s, 3)),
         Trials = sum(inside) / sum(df$Illusion_Type == ill))
}
imap_dfr(illusions, \(label, ill) {
  x <- df[df$Illusion_Type == ill, ]
  bind_rows(
    range_row(ill, range(x$Illusion_Difference), max(abs(x$Illusion_Strength))) |> mutate(Range = "Full"),
    range_row(ill, plot_ranges[[ill]]$difference, max(plot_ranges[[ill]]$strength)) |>
      mutate(Range = "Reliable predictor space"),
    range_row(ill, linear_ranges[[ill]]$difference, linear_ranges[[ill]]$strength) |>
      mutate(Range = "Linear subrange (to be refined)")
  ) |>
    mutate(Illusion = label)
}) |>
  mutate(Illusion = factor(Illusion, levels = illusions)) |>
  select(Illusion, Range, Difference, Strength, Trials) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Illusion") |>
  tab_header(title = "The three ranges of the predictors",
             subtitle = "Full: what the Study 1 models are fitted on. Reliable: what every figure shows. Linear: what Study 2 fits") |>
  cols_label(Range = "", Trials = "Trials") |>
  fmt_percent(Trials, decimals = 1) |>
  gt_style()

in_range <- function(illusion, D, S) {
  r <- linear_ranges[[illusion]]
  if (is.null(r)) return(rep(TRUE, length(D)))
  D >= r$difference[1] - 1e-9 & D <= r$difference[2] + 1e-9 & abs(S) <= r$strength + 1e-9
}

# Every stimulus shown within the range, with its number of trials
stimuli <- df |>
  filter(in_range(first(Illusion_Type), Illusion_Difference, Illusion_Strength),
         .by = Illusion_Type) |>
  count(Illusion_Type, Difference = Illusion_Difference, Strength = Illusion_Strength)

stimuli |>
  summarise(Stimuli = n(), Trials = sum(n), .by = Illusion_Type) |>
  left_join(count(df, Illusion_Type, name = "All"), by = "Illusion_Type") |>
  mutate(Kept = Trials / All,
         Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions)) |>
  arrange(Illusion) |>
  select(Illusion, Stimuli, Trials, All, Kept) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The stimuli fitted",
             subtitle = "Within each illusion's range: distinct stimuli (difference x strength) and trials") |>
  cols_label(Stimuli = "Distinct stimuli", Trials = "Trials", All = "All trials", Kept = "Kept") |>
  fmt_integer(c(Stimuli, Trials, All)) |>
  fmt_percent(Kept, decimals = 1) |>
  gt_style()
```

### How Linear a Coding Is

A coding of the two predictors is judged by how much of each parameter's
surface a linear model in its terms reproduces: the R² of the surface,
on its link scale, regressed on those terms. It is computed in two ways:

- **At the stimuli**, weighted by their number of trials. This is what the
  linear model is fitted to, and the one used for the choices below. The
  stimuli are not spread evenly over the space, so the two differ.
- **Over the grid**, every point weighted the same, as when the Study 1 boxes
  were drawn.

The value at a stimulus is interpolated (bilinearly) between the four grid
points around it. Each coding is summarised by its worst parameter, since the
model is only as linear as its least linear parameter, and by the mean over
the five.

```{r}
# A surface's value at any (S, D), by bilinear interpolation between the four
# grid points around it. `h` is one parameter of one illusion.
surface_at <- function(h, S, D) {
  gx <- sort(unique(h$Illusion_Strength))
  gy <- sort(unique(h$Illusion_Difference))
  z <- matrix(NA_real_, length(gx), length(gy))
  z[cbind(match(h$Illusion_Strength, gx), match(h$Illusion_Difference, gy))] <- h$Link
  i <- pmin(pmax(findInterval(S, gx), 1), length(gx) - 1)
  j <- pmin(pmax(findInterval(D, gy), 1), length(gy) - 1)
  tx <- (S - gx[i]) / (gx[i + 1] - gx[i])
  ty <- (D - gy[j]) / (gy[j + 1] - gy[j])
  z[cbind(i, j)] * (1 - tx) * (1 - ty) + z[cbind(i + 1, j)] * tx * (1 - ty) +
    z[cbind(i, j + 1)] * (1 - tx) * ty + z[cbind(i + 1, j + 1)] * tx * ty
}

# R² of one coding on one illusion, per parameter. A coding is a function of
# the raw difference D and signed strength S that returns the model's terms
# (without the intercept).
linearity <- function(illusion, coding) {
  st <- filter(stimuli, Illusion_Type == illusion)
  map_dfr(names(ddm_links), \(p) {
    h <- filter(surfaces, Illusion_Type == illusion, Parameter == p)
    g <- filter(h, in_range(illusion, Illusion_Difference, Illusion_Strength))
    y <- surface_at(h, st$Strength, st$Difference)
    data.frame(
      Illusion_Type = illusion, Parameter = p,
      R2_trials = summary(lm(y ~ coding(st$Difference, st$Strength), weights = st$n))$r.squared,
      R2_grid = summary(lm(g$Link ~ coding(g$Illusion_Difference, g$Illusion_Strength)))$r.squared
    )
  })
}

# Worst and mean over the parameters
summarise_linearity <- function(r) {
  summarise(r, Worst = min(R2_trials), Worst_Parameter = ddm_labels[Parameter[which.min(R2_trials)]],
            Mean = mean(R2_trials), Worst_Grid = min(R2_grid), Mean_Grid = mean(R2_grid),
            .by = any_of(c("Illusion_Type", "Coding", "Transform_D", "Power_S")))
}
```

### Coding of Illusion Strength

Study 1 coded strength as one signed variable, positive when the illusion
works against the correct answer (conflicting) and negative when it works for
it (facilitating). Three codings are compared:

- **Difference × Strength**: signed strength, one slope across both sides.
- **Difference × Strength × Effect, no gap**: strength in absolute value, and
  whether it is conflicting or facilitating, coded +0.5 / −0.5, which enters
  only through its interactions with strength (`Strength:Effect` and
  `Difference:Strength:Effect`). Each side has its own slope, and the two
  lines meet at zero strength. The value of `Effect` on the trials with no
  illusion does not matter, as it is multiplied by a strength of 0 there.
- **Difference × Strength × Effect, with a gap**: the full product, with
  `Effect` and `Difference:Effect` as well (`Effect` 0 for the trials with no
  illusion), so that the two lines need not meet at zero strength.

```{r}
# +0.5 conflicting, -0.5 facilitating, 0 with no illusion
effect_code <- function(S) 0.5 * sign(S)

codings <- list(
  "Difference × Strength" = \(D, S) cbind(D, S, D * S),
  "Difference × Strength × Effect, no gap" = \(D, S) {
    a <- abs(S); e <- effect_code(S)
    cbind(D, a, D * a, a * e, D * a * e)
  },
  "Difference × Strength × Effect, with a gap" = \(D, S) {
    a <- abs(S); e <- effect_code(S)
    cbind(D, a, e, D * a, D * e, a * e, D * a * e)
  }
)

linearity_codings <- imap_dfr(codings, \(coding, name) {
  map_dfr(names(illusions), \(ill) linearity(ill, coding)) |> mutate(Coding = name)
})

linearity_codings |>
  summarise_linearity() |>
  mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions),
         Coding = factor(Coding, levels = names(codings))) |>
  arrange(Illusion, Coding) |>
  select(Illusion, Coding, Worst, Worst_Parameter, Mean, Worst_Grid, Mean_Grid) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Illusion") |>
  tab_header(title = "Three codings of illusion strength",
             subtitle = "R² of the five DDM-5 surfaces reproduced by a linear model in each coding") |>
  tab_spanner("At the stimuli (trial-weighted)", c(Worst, Worst_Parameter, Mean)) |>
  tab_spanner("Over the grid", c(Worst_Grid, Mean_Grid)) |>
  cols_label(Coding = "", Worst = "Worst", Worst_Parameter = "Worst parameter", Mean = "Mean",
             Worst_Grid = "Worst", Mean_Grid = "Mean") |>
  fmt_number(where(is.numeric), decimals = 3) |>
  colour_r2(c(Worst, Mean, Worst_Grid, Mean_Grid)) |>
  tab_style(cell_text(weight = "bold"),
            cells_body(rows = Coding == "Difference × Strength × Effect, no gap")) |>
  tab_source_note("Bold: the coding retained.") |>
  cols_width(Coding ~ px(300)) |>
  gt_style()
```

Absolute strength with a slope per side is far more linear than signed
strength. The version with a gap at zero strength is the most linear of the
three on all three illusions: the effect of the illusion is steepest at weak
strengths, and two straight lines follow that more closely by not meeting at
zero. The gap is not retained, however (since 2026-11-25; `server/AGENT.md`
§6.15). A weak illusion on one side and a weak illusion on the other are
nearly the same stimulus, and the same one at zero strength, so no parameter
can jump between them: the gap is how straight lines approximate a steep
curve, not a property of the observer. Once fitted, the model is also free to
use it for more than that. The coding retained is the one without the gap.
It costs 0.02 to 0.03 of R² on the worst parameter, the most on the bias of
Vertical-Horizontal, and a transformation of strength that is steep at weak
strengths, such as its square root, gives part of that back (below).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

# Per parameter, for the record
linearity_codings |>
  mutate(Parameter = factor(ddm_labels[Parameter], levels = ddm_labels),
         Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions),
         Coding = factor(Coding, levels = names(codings))) |>
  ggplot(aes(Parameter, R2_trials, fill = Coding)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~Illusion) +
  # The retained coding (no gap) darkest
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", "#1565C0", "#90CAF9")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "R² at the stimuli", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

### Transformations of Difficulty and Strength

The two predictors are physical quantities, whose perceived magnitude need not
be proportional to them, and need not scale in the same way from one illusion
to another. The difference is a Weber fraction in all three illusions: the
size of the larger target relative to the smaller, minus 1 (*Pyllusion*,
`(1 + difference) * size_min`), of the lengths of the lines in Müller-Lyer and
Vertical-Horizontal and of the diameters of the inner circles in Ebbinghaus.
The strength is an angle in Müller-Lyer (of the fins) and Vertical-Horizontal
(of the rotation of one line towards the vertical), and the size of the
surrounding circles relative to the target in Ebbinghaus.

Two kinds of transformation of the difference were searched. Powers, from the
log (the most compressive) to the square, are the empirical family. The log
of the ratio of the two targets, `log(1 + d)`, is the one Weber's law
predicts: if each target is encoded with noise proportional to its size, the
evidence that one is larger grows with the log of their ratio, and the drift
rate with it. Over these ranges it is only mildly compressive (at d = 0.7,
`log(1.7)` = 0.53). The absolute strength was raised to powers from 0.25 to 2.

```{r}
# Transformations of the difference, in order from the most compressive to the
# most expansive, and powers of the absolute strength
transforms_D <- list(
  "log" = log, "0.25" = \(x) x^0.25, "0.5" = sqrt, "log(1 + d)" = log1p,
  "1" = identity, "1.5" = \(x) x^1.5, "2" = \(x) x^2
)
powers_S <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2)

retained_coding <- codings[["Difference × Strength × Effect, no gap"]]
coding_transformed <- function(td, ps) {
  \(D, S) retained_coding(transforms_D[[td]](D), sign(S) * abs(S)^ps)
}

linearity_powers <- expand_grid(Transform_D = names(transforms_D), Power_S = powers_S) |>
  pmap_dfr(\(Transform_D, Power_S) {
    map_dfr(names(illusions), \(ill) linearity(ill, coding_transformed(Transform_D, Power_S))) |>
      mutate(Transform_D = Transform_D, Power_S = Power_S)
  })
summary_powers <- summarise_linearity(linearity_powers)
```

The gains are small, a few hundredths of R² at most, and they are measured on
the surfaces of another model. So the transformations are not chosen here:
the untransformed model is fitted first, and two transformed variants are
fitted after it and compared with it on the data:

- **The best transformation of each illusion.** A transformation counts only
  if it makes the model more linear on both counts, its worst parameter and
  the mean over the five, and only the square root and the two logs, which can
  be stated and reasoned about, are considered. Among those that pass, the one
  with the best worst parameter is the illusion's best.
- **The Weber's-law transformation, `log(1 + d)`, on all three illusions**,
  with absolute strength untransformed: one transformation, with one
  justification, for every illusion.

```{r}
label_D <- c("1" = "Difference", "0.5" = "sqrt(Difference)", "log" = "log(Difference)",
             "log(1 + d)" = "log(1 + Difference)")
label_S <- c("1" = "|Strength|", "0.5" = "sqrt(|Strength|)")

# The candidates: difference as it is, its square root, its log or the log of
# the ratio of the targets, and absolute strength as it is or its square root.
# A transformation is kept if it improves on the untransformed coding in both
# the worst and the mean R² at the stimuli; among those, the best worst R² wins.
candidates <- summary_powers |>
  filter(Transform_D %in% names(label_D), Power_S %in% c(1, 0.5))
untransformed <- filter(candidates, Transform_D == "1", Power_S == 1) |>
  select(Illusion_Type, Worst_None = Worst, Mean_None = Mean, Worst_Parameter_None = Worst_Parameter)

transforms <- candidates |>
  left_join(untransformed, by = "Illusion_Type") |>
  filter((Worst > Worst_None & Mean > Mean_None) | (Transform_D == "1" & Power_S == 1)) |>
  slice_max(Worst, n = 1, by = Illusion_Type) |>
  mutate(Difference = label_D[Transform_D], Strength = label_S[as.character(Power_S)])

transforms |>
  mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions), .before = 1) |>
  arrange(Illusion) |>
  select(Illusion, Difference, Strength, Worst_None, Worst, Mean_None, Mean) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The best transformation of each illusion",
             subtitle = "R² at the stimuli, untransformed and with the best transformation") |>
  tab_spanner("Worst parameter", c(Worst_None, Worst)) |>
  tab_spanner("Mean of the five", c(Mean_None, Mean)) |>
  cols_label(Worst_None = "untransformed", Worst = "best",
             Mean_None = "untransformed", Mean = "best") |>
  fmt_number(where(is.numeric), decimals = 3) |>
  colour_r2(c(Worst_None, Worst, Mean_None, Mean)) |>
  gt_style()
```

Where the gains come from, per parameter: the drift is close to linear
untransformed, and the transformations win on the other parameters (on
Müller-Lyer the bias, the boundary and the drift variability, on
Vertical-Horizontal the bias, on Ebbinghaus the drift variability and the
non-decision time), which no psychophysical law speaks to. On Ebbinghaus, the
best transformation costs the drift 0.03 of R², which the criterion, on the
worst parameter and the mean, lets through. The Weber's-law transformation of
the difference gains about a quarter to a third of what the best one does on
Vertical-Horizontal and Ebbinghaus, and nothing on Müller-Lyer.

```{r}
# Per parameter: untransformed, the transformation retained, and the
# Weber's-law transformation of the difference (with |Strength|)
per_parameter <- function(td, ps, name) {
  linearity_powers |>
    filter(Transform_D == td, Power_S == ps) |>
    select(Illusion_Type, Parameter, R2_trials) |>
    rename(!!name := R2_trials)
}
# Each illusion's group is named after the transformation retained for it
group_label <- with(transforms, setNames(paste0(illusions[Illusion_Type], ": ", Difference, ", ", Strength),
                                         Illusion_Type))
retained <- transforms |>
  select(Illusion_Type, Transform_D, Power_S) |>
  pmap_dfr(\(Illusion_Type, Transform_D, Power_S) {
    ill <- Illusion_Type
    per_parameter(Transform_D, Power_S, "Retained") |> filter(Illusion_Type == ill)
  })

per_parameter("1", 1, "None") |>
  left_join(retained, by = c("Illusion_Type", "Parameter")) |>
  left_join(per_parameter("log(1 + d)", 1, "Weber"), by = c("Illusion_Type", "Parameter")) |>
  mutate(Change_Best = Retained - None,
         Change_Weber = Weber - None,
         Illusion = factor(group_label[Illusion_Type], levels = group_label[names(illusions)]),
         Parameter = factor(ddm_labels[Parameter], levels = ddm_labels)) |>
  arrange(Illusion, Parameter) |>
  select(Illusion, Parameter, None, Retained, Change_Best, Weber, Change_Weber) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Illusion") |>
  tab_header(title = "Where the gains come from",
             subtitle = "R² at the stimuli, per parameter, and its change from the untransformed coding") |>
  tab_spanner("Best transformation", c(Retained, Change_Best)) |>
  tab_spanner("log(1 + Difference)", c(Weber, Change_Weber)) |>
  cols_label(Parameter = "", None = "Untransformed", Retained = "R²", Change_Best = "Change",
             Weber = "R²", Change_Weber = "Change") |>
  fmt_number(where(is.numeric), decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_number(starts_with("Change"), decimals = 3, force_sign = TRUE) |>
  colour_r2(c(None, Retained, Weber)) |>
  colour_change(starts_with("Change")) |>
  tab_source_note(paste("Best transformation: the illusion's best (in its group's title).",
                        "log(1 + Difference): the Weber's-law transformation, with |Strength| untransformed.")) |>
  gt_style()
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4

plot_powers <- function(summary_powers, transforms, base_size = 9, label_size = base_size / 3.6) {
  d <- summary_powers |>
    mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions),
           Transform_D = factor(Transform_D, levels = names(transforms_D)),
           Power_S = factor(Power_S, levels = powers_S))
  chosen <- transforms |>
    mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions),
           Transform_D = factor(Transform_D, levels = names(transforms_D)),
           Power_S = factor(Power_S, levels = powers_S))
  ggplot(d, aes(Power_S, Transform_D)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = Worst), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    # Untransformed (dotted) and the illusion's best (solid)
    geom_tile(data = filter(d, Transform_D == "1", Power_S == "1"), fill = NA, colour = "black",
              linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_tile(data = chosen, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", Worst)),
                  colour = Worst < quantile(Worst, 0.4)), size = label_size) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C", name = "Worst R²") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "black", "FALSE" = "white"), guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~Illusion) +
    labs(x = "Power of absolute strength", y = "Transformation of difference") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
          legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.5, "cm"))
}
plot_powers(summary_powers, transforms)
```

The search over the full grid lands near the best transformations: nothing
outside the candidates does much better, so limiting them to the square root
and the logs costs little.

### The Interval Before the Stimulus

The interstimulus interval (ISI) is how long the fixation cross stayed on
screen before the stimulus: a foreperiod. It was drawn on every trial from a
uniform distribution 0.5 s wide, whose position depended on the study.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3

# The centre of each study's window, which the ISI is centred on below
isi_windows <- df |>
  summarise(ISI_min = min(ISI), ISI_max = max(ISI), .by = Dataset) |>
  mutate(ISI_centre = (ISI_min + ISI_max) / 2)

df |>
  filter(Illusion_Type == "MullerLyer") |>
  summarise(Participants = n_distinct(Participant), Trials = n(), .by = Dataset) |>
  left_join(isi_windows, by = "Dataset") |>
  arrange(ISI_min, Dataset) |>
  mutate(Dataset = sub("^IllusionGame", "", Dataset)) |>
  select(Dataset, ISI_min, ISI_max, ISI_centre, Participants, Trials) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "ISI by study", subtitle = "Müller-Lyer, in seconds") |>
  tab_spanner("ISI window", starts_with("ISI")) |>
  cols_label(Dataset = "Study", ISI_min = "from", ISI_max = "to", ISI_centre = "centre") |>
  fmt_number(starts_with("ISI"), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_integer(c(Participants, Trials)) |>
  gt_style()

df |>
  filter(Illusion_Type == "MullerLyer") |>
  ggplot(aes(ISI, fill = Dataset)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "ISI (s)", y = "Trials (Müller-Lyer)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Its effect is that of a variable foreperiod. Within every study, the longer the
wait within its window, the faster the correct responses, levelling off
towards the end, while the error rate does not change. From the shortest wait
to the longest, the median RT fell by 26 to 37 ms in five of the seven
studies, by 10 ms in Self-Association, the smallest, and by 5 ms in the EEG
study, whose window came latest (1.0–1.5 s). As the wait goes on, the stimulus becomes more
likely to come next, and participants more prepared for it. What matters is
where the ISI falls within its study's window, not its absolute value: a
second is the end of the window in Validation and the start of it in the EEG
study.

```{r}
# Median RT of the correct responses (all illusions) by where the ISI falls in
# its study's window, in fifths of the window
df |>
  left_join(isi_windows, by = "Dataset") |>
  mutate(Position = cut((ISI - ISI_centre) / 0.25, c(-1.01, -0.6, -0.2, 0.2, 0.6, 1.01),
                        labels = c("Shortest", "Short", "Middle", "Long", "Longest")),
         Dataset = sub("^IllusionGame", "", Dataset)) |>
  filter(Error == 0) |>
  summarise(RT = 1000 * median(RT), .by = c(Dataset, ISI_min, Position)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Position, values_from = RT) |>
  arrange(ISI_min, Dataset) |>
  mutate(Change = Longest - Shortest) |>
  select(Dataset, Shortest, Short, Middle, Long, Longest, Change) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The foreperiod effect",
             subtitle = "Median RT of correct responses (ms), by the position of the ISI in its study's window") |>
  tab_spanner("Position of the ISI in the window", Shortest:Longest) |>
  cols_label(Dataset = "Study", Change = "Longest − shortest") |>
  fmt_number(Shortest:Longest, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(Change, decimals = 0, force_sign = TRUE) |>
  data_color(Shortest:Longest, fn = squished(c("#E3F2FD", "#1565C0"), c(590, 680))) |>
  gt_style()
```

ISI therefore enters the model centred on its study's window,
`(ISI - centre) / 0.25`, from −1 at the start of the window to 1 at its end in
every study. Its effect is then estimated only from the variation within each
study, which was randomised from trial to trial, and is not confounded with
the study, nor extrapolated beyond the range a study covers (above 1.1 s, the
absolute ISI comes from the EEG study alone). The absolute level of each
window is taken up by the study's intercept (below), with everything else
that differs between studies.

It enters every parameter, the outlier proportion included, as a quadratic,
`poly(ISI, 2, raw = TRUE)`, for the levelling off: the two terms are then ISI
and its square in these units, whose slopes the priors of the other predictors
suit, and which need no basis carried over to predict new values. An
orthogonal `poly(ISI, 2)` would not do: its columns have a length of 1 whatever
the unit of ISI, so a standard deviation of about 0.002 on 200,000 trials,
against which the slope priors would hold the effect of ISI near zero, and
differently for every number of trials.

### The Studies

The seven studies differ in their settings, samples and procedures (overall
error rates from 18% to 24%), and every participant took part in one of them.
Each parameter, the outlier proportion included, gets a random intercept per
study, `(1 | Study)`. The participants' own effects are then deviations from
their study's mean rather than from the grand mean, which matters for the
correlations between illusions: without it, the differences between studies
would be shared by a participant's effects on all three illusions, and inflate
their correlations. With seven studies, it is kept to intercepts.

```{r}
df |>
  summarise(Participants = n_distinct(Participant), Trials = n(), Error = mean(Error, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = Dataset) |>
  arrange(desc(Participants)) |>
  mutate(Dataset = sub("^IllusionGame", "", Dataset)) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The studies", subtitle = "All three illusions") |>
  cols_label(Dataset = "Study", Error = "Error rate") |>
  fmt_integer(c(Participants, Trials)) |>
  fmt_percent(Error, decimals = 1) |>
  gt_style()
```

### The Model

```{r}
# The predictors as fit_model.R makes them, per illusion, from the range above:
# - Difference: the difference (transformed, in the variants), rescaled from
#   -1 to 1 over the range
# - Strength: the absolute strength (transformed, in the variants), divided by
#   its largest value in the range (0 to 1)
# - Effect: +0.5 conflicting, -0.5 facilitating, 0 with no illusion (it only
#   enters multiplied by Strength, which is 0 there)
# - ISI: (ISI - centre of the study's window) / 0.25, -1 to 1
# The model fitted first is untransformed; the two variants are fitted after it.
transforms |>
  mutate(Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions),
         Best = paste0(Difference, ", ", Strength),
         Weber = "log(1 + Difference), |Strength|",
         Difference_from = map_dbl(Illusion_Type, \(ill) min(stimuli$Difference[stimuli$Illusion_Type == ill])),
         Difference_to = map_dbl(Illusion_Type, \(ill) max(stimuli$Difference[stimuli$Illusion_Type == ill])),
         Strength_max = map_dbl(Illusion_Type, \(ill) max(abs(stimuli$Strength[stimuli$Illusion_Type == ill])))) |>
  arrange(Illusion) |>
  select(Illusion, Difference_from, Difference_to, Strength_max, Best, Weber) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "The predictors of each illusion",
             subtitle = "The range of raw values fitted, and the transformations of the two variants") |>
  tab_spanner("Range fitted", c(Difference_from, Difference_to, Strength_max)) |>
  tab_spanner("Transformed variants", c(Best, Weber)) |>
  cols_label(Difference_from = "Difference from", Difference_to = "to", Strength_max = "Strength (±)",
             Best = "Best", Weber = "Weber's law") |>
  fmt_number(c(Difference_from, Difference_to), decimals = 3, drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE) |>
  fmt_number(Strength_max, decimals = 2, drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE) |>
  gt_style()
```

The same formula for the five parameters of DDM-5 (`lin_ddm5` in
`server/models.R`), with every effect varying by participant and an intercept
varying by study:

```r
# The same terms on every parameter:
#   Difference * Strength + Strength:Effect + Difference:Strength:Effect
brms::bf(
  RT | dec(Error) ~ Difference * Strength + Strength:Effect + Difference:Strength:Effect +
                    poly(ISI, 2, raw = TRUE) +
                    (1 + Difference * Strength + Strength:Effect + Difference:Strength:Effect | Participant) +
                    (1 | Study),
  boundary        ~ ...,  # the same
  bias            ~ ...,
  ndt             ~ ...,
  sigmadrift      ~ ...,
  sigmabias = 0,
  sigmandt = 0,
  poutlier        ~ poly(ISI, 2, raw = TRUE) + (1 | Participant) + (1 | Study),
  family = cogmod::cogmod_ddm()
)
```

With absolute strength and its side coded ±0.5, entering only through its
interactions with strength, the coefficients read: the intercept is the
parameter at zero strength, where the two sides meet; `Strength:Effect` is
the difference between the conflicting and the facilitating slope, i.e. the
sensitivity to the illusion; `Strength` is their mean, i.e. how much more (or
less) a conflicting illusion hurts than a facilitating one helps; and each
`Difference:` term is how one of these changes with task difficulty.
`Strength:Effect` is also half the signed strength, so the model is Study 1's
signed coding with a V-shaped term in absolute strength added.

## The Linear Approximation

How closely the linear models follow the DDM-5 surfaces of Study 1: the figure
of the retained model in `2_modelcomparison.qmd`, its observable outcomes and
its parameters along illusion strength, one curve per level of task
difficulty, with the linear model's predictions over it as dashed lines. Both
are population-level predictions at the same points (`compute_curves()` in
`server/predictions.R`), the linear model's at the centre of each study's ISI
window. With strength coded as its absolute value and its side, the linear
model's curves are two half-lines, one per side, which meet at zero strength.
For now these are tests on 50 participants, of Müller-Lyer and
Vertical-Horizontal (`server/AGENT.md` §6.15); Ebbinghaus has none yet.

Each illusion is drawn over its reliable predictor space: DDM-5 over all of
it, and a linear model over the range it was fitted on, so that a model fitted
on a narrower subrange shows as dashed lines that stop short of the edges.

```{r}
# The curves of Study 1's DDM-5 (one file per illusion) and of the linear
# models that have been fitted, in raw units, with the family's parameter names
approx_labels <- c("Error Rate" = "Error Rate", "Median RT" = "Median RT", ddm_labels)

# DDM-5's curves over the reliable predictor space (a file made over a wider
# range is cropped to it)
gam_curves <- imap_dfr(illusions, \(label, ill) {
  p <- readRDS(paste0(pred_path, "gam_ddm5_", tolower(ill), "_", ill, ".rds"))
  if (!covers_plot_range(p$meta$plot_range, ill)) {
    message("DDM-5 on ", ill, ": the predictions do not cover all of plot_ranges; re-run `./hpc predict`.")
  }
  crop_to_plot_range(p$curves, ill) |>
    restore_units(ill) |>
    mutate(Effect = NA_real_)
})

linear_files <- linear_files[file.exists(linear_files)]
linear_curves <- imap_dfr(linear_files, \(file, ill) {
  p <- readRDS(file)
  if (!identical(p$meta$version, igc_predictions_version)) {
    stop(file, " is format ", p$meta$version, " and this script reads ", igc_predictions_version,
         ": re-run `./hpc predict`.")
  }
  # The linear model's curves are in raw units already
  # (restore_linear_units())
  mutate(p$curves, Illusion_Type = ill)
})
if (length(linear_files) < length(illusions)) {
  message("No linear model yet for: ", paste(setdiff(names(illusions), names(linear_files)), collapse = ", "))
}

approx_curves <- bind_rows(gam_curves, linear_curves) |>
  filter(Parameter %in% names(approx_labels)) |>
  select(Illusion_Type, Type, Illusion_Difference, Illusion_Strength, Effect, Parameter, Predicted)
```

```{r}
# The figure of the retained model in 2_modelcomparison.qmd (plot_retained()),
# with the linear models' curves over the GAM's, dashed, in the colour of their
# difficulty level. Drift and starting point are turned around as there: the
# fits code an error as the upper boundary, so their drift is negative towards
# the correct response and their bias is the distance of the starting point
# from the correct boundary. Here the drift is positive towards the correct
# response, and the starting point is 0 at the error boundary and 1 at the
# correct one.
plot_approximation <- function(curves) {
  # The rows, in two groups: what can be observed, and what the model explains
  # it with
  groups <- list(
    "Observable Outcomes" = c("Error Rate" = "Error rate", "Median RT" = "Median RT\n(correct, s)"),
    "Model Parameters" = c("Drift" = "Drift rate\n(+ towards correct)", "Drift Variability" = "Drift rate\nvariability",
                           "Boundary" = "Boundary\nseparation", "Bias" = "Starting point\n(0 error, 1 correct)",
                           "NDT" = "Non-decision\ntime (s)")
  )
  panels <- unlist(unname(groups))

  # The difficulty levels differ between illusions: each curve is coloured by
  # its difference, on a scale from the hardest of the GAM's levels (0) to the
  # easiest (1), which are evenly spaced. A linear curve at the same level as a
  # GAM curve takes its colour, and one predicted on another grid (made before
  # plot_ranges last changed) the colour of its own difficulty.
  range_of <- curves |>
    filter(Type == "GAM") |>
    summarise(Lo = min(Illusion_Difference), Hi = max(Illusion_Difference), .by = Illusion_Type)
  d <- curves |>
    left_join(range_of, by = "Illusion_Type") |>
    mutate(Difficulty = pmin(pmax((Illusion_Difference - Lo) / (Hi - Lo), 0), 1),
           Predicted = case_when(Parameter == "mu" ~ -Predicted,
                                 Parameter == "bias" ~ 1 - Predicted,
                                 .default = Predicted),
           Parameter = panels[approx_labels[as.character(Parameter)]],
           Illusion = factor(illusions[Illusion_Type], levels = illusions),
           Type = factor(Type, levels = c("GAM", "Linear")),
           # One line per level for the GAM, per level and side for the
           # linear model
           Line = paste(Type, round(Illusion_Difference, 5), sign(coalesce(Effect, 0))))

  # Reference lines: no drift, and a starting point half-way. Dotted, where
  # plot_retained() has them dashed, which here are the linear models.
  refs <- data.frame(Parameter = panels[c("Drift", "Bias")], y = c(0, 0.5))

  # Each illusion's x-axis over its reliable predictor space, whatever is
  # drawn on it: an invisible point at each end, in every row, at a value the
  # row already has
  ends <- d |>
    filter(!is.na(Predicted)) |>
    summarise(Predicted = first(Predicted), .by = c(Illusion_Type, Illusion, Parameter)) |>
    cross_join(data.frame(Side = c(-1, 1))) |>
    mutate(Illusion_Strength = map2_dbl(Illusion_Type, Side, \(ill, s) s * max(plot_ranges[[ill]]$strength)))

  # One group of rows. The groups are plots of their own, one above the other,
  # so that there is a gap between them. Their columns line up, so the
  # illusions are named once, above the first, and the axis of illusion
  # strength is drawn once, under the last.
  block <- function(name) {
    rows <- groups[[name]]
    first <- name == names(groups)[1]
    last <- name == names(groups)[length(groups)]
    in_block <- \(x) mutate(filter(x, Parameter %in% rows), Parameter = factor(Parameter, levels = rows))
    ggplot(in_block(d), aes(Illusion_Strength, Predicted)) +
      geom_blank(data = in_block(ends)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_hline(data = in_block(refs), aes(yintercept = y), colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.4,
                 linetype = "dotted") +
      geom_line(aes(colour = Difficulty, group = Line, linetype = Type, linewidth = Type), na.rm = TRUE) +
      scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("#D84315", "#FF9800", "#FFC107", "#8BC34A", "#2E7D32"),
                             limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 1), labels = c("hardest", "easiest"),
                             guide = guide_colourbar(title.position = "left", barwidth = grid::unit(6, "lines"),
                                                     barheight = grid::unit(0.5, "lines"), order = 1)) +
      scale_linetype_manual(values = c(GAM = "solid", Linear = "22"), drop = FALSE,
                            labels = c(GAM = "GAM (Study 1)", Linear = "Linear (Study 2)"),
                            guide = guide_legend(title = NULL, order = 2,
                                                 override.aes = list(colour = "grey25"))) +
      scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(GAM = 0.55, Linear = 0.5), guide = "none") +
      facet_grid(Parameter ~ Illusion, scales = "free", switch = "y") +
      labs(y = NULL, colour = "Task difficulty ",
           x = if (last) "Illusion strength (negative: congruent, positive: incongruent)") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
      theme(strip.placement = "outside",
            strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 8, lineheight = 0.9),
            strip.text.x = if (first) element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5) else element_blank(),
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.25),
            panel.spacing = grid::unit(7, "pt"),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
            axis.text.x = if (last) element_text(size = 7) else element_blank(),
            legend.title = element_text(size = 8, vjust = 0.9),
            legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5),
            legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.6, "lines"),
            legend.margin = margin(t = -4),
            plot.margin = margin(if (first) 4 else 9, 4, 4, 2))
  }

  # The name of a group, written upwards on a band at the left of its rows.
  # patchwork lines its panel up with the panels of the group, so the band is
  # as tall as the rows and no taller.
  band <- function(name) {
    first <- name == names(groups)[1]
    ggplot() +
      annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = name, angle = 90, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3, colour = "grey15") +
      theme_void() +
      theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey91", colour = NA),
            plot.margin = margin(if (first) 4 else 9, 0, 4, 2))
  }

  wrap_plots(unlist(lapply(names(groups), \(name) list(band(name), block(name))), recursive = FALSE),
             ncol = 2, widths = c(0.035, 1), heights = lengths(groups), guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

#| fig-height: 8.5

plot_approximation(approx_curves)

## The Effect of the Interval Before the Stimulus

What the linear models make of the ISI (see "The Interval Before the
Stimulus" above). Each parameter has the same quadratic in the position of
the ISI within its study's window, plus a random intercept per study. The
curves below are each study's, with its own intercept and the participant at
the population level, along its own window in seconds: the window's centre
plus 0.25 s times the coded ISI, as `fit_model.R` codes it. They are drawn
at three stimuli: no illusion, at the hardest, the middle and the easiest
difficulty of the range fitted. On the link scale the ISI moves every
parameter by the same amount at every stimulus, so a parameter's curves
differ between the three columns only in their level; the error rate and the
median RT depend on the stimulus too. As in the figure of the linear
approximation, the drift is positive towards the correct response and the
starting point runs from 0 at the error boundary to 1 at the correct one.

The predictions are made on the cluster (`compute_isi_curves()` in
`server/predictions.R`) and stored in the linear models' prediction files,
since 2026-11-25. For now only the 50-participant tests of the Müller-Lyer
and Vertical-Horizontal models have them (`server/AGENT.md` §6.15), whose
studies are those their 50 participants come from: the study intercepts of the studies with few of them
rest on little.

```{r}
# The ISI predictions of the linear models that have them, with the ISI in
# seconds: the centre of its study's window (isi_windows, computed as
# fit_model.R does) + 0.25 x the coded ISI
isi <- imap(linear_files, \(file, ill) readRDS(file)$isi)
if (any(vapply(isi, is.null, logical(1)))) {
  message("No ISI predictions (re-run `./hpc predict`) for: ",
          paste(names(isi)[vapply(isi, is.null, logical(1))], collapse = ", "))
}
isi <- isi[!vapply(isi, is.null, logical(1))]

isi_curves <- imap_dfr(isi, \(x, ill) mutate(x$curves, Illusion_Type = ill)) |>
  left_join(select(isi_windows, Study = Dataset, ISI_centre), by = "Study") |>
  mutate(ISI_seconds = ISI_centre + 0.25 * ISI,
         Study = factor(sub("^IllusionGame", "", Study), levels = study_order))
stopifnot(!anyNA(isi_curves$ISI_seconds))

study_colours <- c(Validation = "#E91E63", EEG = "#9C27B0", Reliability = "#3F51B5",
                   International = "#03A9F4", Suggestibility = "#009688", PCS = "#8BC34A",
                   SelfAssociation = "#FF9800")

# One illusion: a row per outcome and parameter, a column per stimulus, a line
# per study along its own window
plot_isi <- function(curves, illusion) {
  rows <- c("Error Rate" = "Error rate", "Median RT" = "Median RT\n(correct, s)",
            "Drift" = "Drift rate\n(+ towards correct)", "Drift Variability" = "Drift rate\nvariability",
            "Boundary" = "Boundary\nseparation", "Bias" = "Starting point\n(0 error, 1 correct)",
            "NDT" = "Non-decision\ntime (s)")
  d <- curves |>
    filter(Illusion_Type == illusion, Parameter %in% names(approx_labels)) |>
    mutate(Predicted = case_when(Parameter == "mu" ~ -Predicted,
                                 Parameter == "bias" ~ 1 - Predicted,
                                 .default = Predicted),
           Row = factor(rows[approx_labels[as.character(Parameter)]], levels = rows))
  levels_d <- sort(unique(d$Illusion_Difference))
  d$Column <- factor(paste0(c("Hardest", "Middle", "Easiest")[match(d$Illusion_Difference, levels_d)],
                            " (difference ", signif(d$Illusion_Difference, 3), ")"))
  d$Column <- factor(d$Column, levels = unique(d$Column[order(d$Illusion_Difference)]))
  ggplot(d, aes(ISI_seconds, Predicted, colour = Study)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
    # Each panel its own y-axis: a parameter's level differs between the
    # stimuli far more than the ISI moves it
    ggh4x::facet_grid2(Row ~ Column, scales = "free_y", independent = "y", switch = "y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = study_colours, drop = TRUE) +
    labs(x = "ISI (s)", y = NULL, colour = "Study",
         title = paste0(illusions[[illusion]], ": the effect of the ISI, with no illusion")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1),
          panel.spacing.y = unit(0.8, "lines"), legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 10

for (ill in names(isi)) print(plot_isi(isi_curves, ill))
```

In the 50-participant test (Müller-Lyer, 2026-11-25), the model reproduces
the foreperiod effect of the data. The median RT of correct responses falls by
about 30 ms over the first half of the window and then levels off, as in the
table above. It does so mostly through the boundary separation, the one
coefficient whose interval excludes zero (narrower at the end of the window
than at its start), and the non-decision time, which is shortest about three
quarters of the way through the window. The drift barely moves. With the
narrower boundary, the error rate at the hardest stimulus rises by a few
points, which the data do not show at the level of the whole study. The
error-rate panels at the middle and easiest stimuli are simulation noise
around rates of 1% and 0.2%. All of this rests on 50 participants, and the
study intercepts on fewer still.

The coefficients themselves, on each parameter's link scale, per unit of the
coded ISI (0.25 s, half the window): the linear and the quadratic
term, and the change from the start of the window to its end (twice the
linear term; the quadratic term is the same at both ends), with the standard
deviation of the study intercepts for comparison. Medians and 95% intervals
of the posterior. The drift's and the starting point's are turned around as
in the figure: positive towards the correct response.

```{r}
# The ISI coefficients (b_<dpar>_polyISI2rawEQTRUE1 and 2) and the SDs of the
# study intercepts (sd_Study__<dpar>_Intercept), per parameter
isi_coefficients <- imap_dfr(isi, \(x, ill) mutate(x$coefficients, Illusion_Type = ill)) |>
  rename(Low = `2.5%`, High = `97.5%`) |>
  mutate(
    Dpar = case_when(
      startsWith(variable, "sd_Study__") ~ sub("_?Intercept$", "", sub("^sd_Study__", "", variable)),
      .default = sub("_?polyISI.*$", "", sub("^b_", "", variable))),
    Dpar = if_else(Dpar == "", "mu", Dpar),
    Term = case_when(startsWith(variable, "sd_Study__") ~ "SD_Study",
                     endsWith(variable, "1") ~ "ISI",
                     .default = "ISI2"),
    # Turned around, for the drift and the starting point (the bias's logit
    # changes sign with 1 - bias), as in the figure; not their SDs
    Flip = Dpar %in% c("mu", "bias") & Term != "SD_Study",
    across(c(median, Low, High), \(x) if_else(Flip, -x, x)),
    Low2 = if_else(Flip, High, Low), High = if_else(Flip, Low, High), Low = Low2)

fmt_ci <- \(m, lo, hi) sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", m, lo, hi)
isi_coefficients |>
  mutate(Cell = fmt_ci(median, Low, High)) |>
  select(Illusion_Type, Dpar, Term, Cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Term, values_from = Cell) |>
  left_join(isi_coefficients |>
              filter(Term == "ISI") |>
              transmute(Illusion_Type, Dpar, Change = fmt_ci(2 * median, 2 * Low, 2 * High)),
            by = c("Illusion_Type", "Dpar")) |>
  mutate(Illusion = illusions[Illusion_Type],
         Parameter = c(ddm_labels, poutlier = "Outlier proportion")[Dpar],
         Parameter = factor(Parameter, levels = c("Drift", "Drift Variability", "Boundary", "Bias", "NDT",
                                                  "Outlier proportion"))) |>
  arrange(Illusion, Parameter) |>
  select(Illusion, Parameter, ISI, ISI2, Change, SD_Study) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Illusion") |>
  tab_header(title = "The ISI coefficients",
             subtitle = "Link scale, per 0.25 s (half the window); median [95% interval]") |>
  cols_label(ISI = "ISI", ISI2 = "ISI²", Change = "Start to end of the window",
             SD_Study = "SD of the study intercepts") |>
  gt_style()
```

## Figures for the Paper

The figures of Study 2 in `paper/manuscript.qmd`, saved to `paper/figures/`,
as in `2_modelcomparison.qmd`: the manuscript includes the files and computes
nothing itself. Since 2026-11-25 there is one: the figure of the
specification (the codings and the transformations, `study2_specification.png`)
was dropped from the paper, whose Methods give its results in the text. They
are the tables of "Coding of Illusion Strength" and "Transformations of
Difficulty and Strength" above.

```{r}
paper_dir <- if (dir.exists("../paper")) "../paper/figures/" else "paper/figures/"
save_figure <- function(plot, name, width, height) {
  dir.create(paper_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  ggsave(paste0(paper_dir, name, ".png"), plot, width = width, height = height,
         dpi = 300, bg = "white", device = ragg::agg_png)
  plot
}
```
